label: IoT Sensor Simulator
info:
Generates one simulated sensor reading every second and POSTs it straight to the Express backend. No preprocessing happens here — Node-RED's only job is telemetry generation.

Flow:  inject (1s) -> function (generate) -> http request (POST /api/data) -> debug
                                                    |-> catch (on failure) -> retry function -> delay -> back to http request

All preprocessing (physics validation, buffering, missing-data detection, Hampel-filter outlier capping, one-minute aggregation, data-quality scoring) now runs server-side in server/preprocessing/ (see pipeline.js), triggered by every POST /api/data request.

RETRY QUEUE: the http request node used to fail silently (senderr: false, no error handling) — a backend restart or transient network blip would drop that tick's reading with no trace. senderr is now true, routed to a Catch node scoped to this http request node, which feeds a retry function (adds/increments msg.retryCount, gives up after 3 attempts) and a delay node (1s backoff) that re-sends the SAME reading back into the http request node. This does not eliminate gaps entirely (a sustained outage longer than ~3 seconds still drops readings), but it absorbs the transient failures a fire-and-forget POST previously lost outright.

NOTE on the http request node's URL: this flow now runs as the node-red service in the single-CT docker-compose.yml, which uses network_mode: host for every service (see that file's top-of-file note), so the URL is http://127.0.0.1:3000/api/data -- this bypasses Traefik/Authentik entirely by design (machine-to-machine ingestion, not an interactive session, unchanged from the prior split-CT deployment). Running this flow.json somewhere else (native npx node-red, a different container) means editing this URL back to whatever actually reaches port 3000 from there.
